title: Pilot POS Operating Manual
summary: How Pelagos uses Pilot: cashless payments and tips, waitron and manager POS procedures, the daily control cycle, stock takes, cash-up and Day End, and month-end reporting.
body:
## 1. PURPOSE OF THIS MANUAL

This manual gives Pelagos a written operating standard for the Pilot routines that affect front-of-house ordering, payment reconciliation, stock control, food cost, beverage cost and month-end reporting. Its objective is to turn Pilot’s training modules, setup guides and short training videos into practical, auditable procedures that staff and managers can follow the same way every time.

| **Area**                     | **Outcome this manual is meant to protect**                                                                                                    |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Front-of-house POS use**   | Orders, splits, transfers, discounts and voids are rung up correctly and authorised, so bills, stock and reports stay accurate.                |
| **Cashless payment control** | Every payment is closed with the right payment type, tips are paid over in full and every cash-up variance is explained.                       |
| **Daily bar controls**       | Detect shrinkage, over-pouring, free issues, ringing errors and missed captures quickly.                                                       |
| **Weekly kitchen controls**  | Track food cost movement, wastage, recipe compliance and stock discipline.                                                                     |
| **Month-end stock**          | Produce reliable stock valuations and credible management accounts.                                                                            |
| **System setup**             | Keep Pilot categories, Master File items, recipes, stock points, prep links, PLUs, screens and costings accurate so reports remain meaningful. |
| **GM reporting**             | Ensure variances are investigated, explained and escalated with an action trail.                                                               |

## 2. CORE PILOT PRINCIPLES THAT PELAGOS MUST WORK AROUND

- **Pelagos is cashless.** We never take cash from a customer, so no cash is kept in any till, no float is issued and Pilot’s cash functions (cash tender, floats, cash payouts and staff IOUs or loans) are not used. See section 5.
- Garbage in, garbage out: Pilot’s own admin training stresses that poor source data produces poor reporting and obsolete information.
- The Master File is the starting point of the system. Every purchase, stock, portion, recipe and expense item must exist there before it is used anywhere else in Pilot.
- The Prep Sheet is a daily control sheet and one of the most valuable daily stock control tools in Pilot.
- The Stock Count Sheet gives a snapshot of back stock and is designed for regular weekly reconciliation.
- PLU Costings and recipe setup drive theoretical and raw material usage reporting; inaccurate recipes make those reports unreliable.
- Admin Cashup is meant to reconcile the full trading period after waitrons and POS stations have already been cashed off. At Pelagos it reconciles card and other non-cash payment types and retained tips, never cash.
- Day End should only be run after open tables are closed and all required daily routines have been completed. Nothing may be captured for the next trading day before Day End has been run.

## 3. PELAGOS ROLE OWNERSHIP

| **Role**                   | **Main Pilot responsibilities**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Waitrons and bar staff** | Log in with their own fingerprint, open tables with the correct covers, ring up and order items correctly, take payment through TABBS and never accept cash.                                                                                                                                |
| **Bar team**               | Count bar front stock daily and record quantities on the bar count sheet.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Closing Duty Manager**   | Authorise voids, discounts and transfers, close non-TABBS payments with the correct payment type, cash off waitrons, complete the Admin Cashup (payment types and retained tips), review the daily bar count, capture it in Pilot, review variances, run Day End and submit the daily pack. |
| **Head Chef**              | Control kitchen daily issues, production, bulk portioning and prep discipline, perform the Sunday 17:00 kitchen stock take, capture the stock in Pilot and submit the weekly pack.                                                                                                          |
| **FOH Manager**            | Complete the monthly FOH small-assets count and sign off losses, breakages and replacements.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **F&B Administrator**      | Review and verify month-end bar and kitchen stock files, capture or validate the final month-end stock, review variances, compile the monthly cash-up workbook and the GM report pack and submit final month-end reporting.                                                                 |
| **General Manager**        | Act as Pilot site operator, or delegate in writing: control user access and passwords, approve setup changes and hold the PilotLive owner or admin rights. Review the monthly control pack, query abnormal losses and approve corrective actions.                                           |

## 5. CASHLESS TRADING, PAYMENT TYPES AND TIPS

> **Pelagos cashless rule.** We are cashless and will never take any cash from a customer. No cash is kept in any till, no float is issued and no cash payout, IOU or staff loan is processed in Pilot. If a guest offers cash, politely explain that Pelagos is cashless and offer card payment.

### How a normal day works

- Guests order and pay through the day, mostly by card on the TABBS machine, sometimes with a tip added.
- When a bill is paid through TABBS and everything works, TABBS closes the table automatically. The other payment options below are only for payments that do not go through TABBS.
- At close, the Closing Duty Manager works through the cash-up checklist in section 12, including typing in each staff member’s tip total, because Pelagos pays staff 100% of their tips. This manual step is where small differences creep in.
- Day End then produces the Day End report, a full record of everything that happened, and resets the POS for the next day’s trade.
- If the POS report and the manually entered figures (once tips are accounted for) do not match the day’s actual food and drink sales, the Notes column of the monthly cash-up workbook explains why (section 23).

### Payment types on the POS

| **Payment type**         | **When it is used**                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **TABBS**                | The POS name for a card payment on the restaurant’s main card machine. This is the normal way most money comes in, and TABBS closes the table automatically.                                        |
| **Tabbs Manual**         | TABBS took the payment but failed to close the table automatically. Tabbs Manual closes the table while still showing it was paid via TABBS. Never take the payment a second time.                  |
| **Credit Card (C/CARD)** | The TABBS machines are down, so payment is taken on the Forever Facilities FNB card machine (the backup machine) and entered manually.                                                              |
| **EFT**                  | Payment received by bank transfer, typically for events or functions. Payments toward a customer account are also made by EFT.                                                                      |
| **Customer Account**     | Guests, usually owners, who keep a monthly account instead of paying per visit.                                                                                                                     |
| **MaxiClub**             | Paid with a MaxiClub voucher. Follow PEL-MAN-002 MaxiClub POS User Guide once MaxiClub goes live.                                                                                                   |
| **Voucher**              | Paid with a voucher Pelagos issued manually as a prize. No money is received, but the items must still be rung up so Pilot deducts the stock and the stock is not short. This should happen rarely. |
| **Dineplan**             | Event pre-payments made through Dineplan, which Dineplan then pays over to Pelagos by EFT. See PEL-SOP-003 Dineplan Reservations.                                                                   |

### Payment types and Pilot functions Pelagos does not use

| **Item**                     | **Rule at Pelagos**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **CASH**                     | We are cashless and will never take any cash from a customer. A cash figure on any report is an error and must be investigated.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **CHEQUE**                   | Never an actual cheque. Until now it was used as a placeholder to close a bill while a guest whose card was declined arranged another way to pay, usually EFT. It is not one of the payment options going forward: close the bill with the payment type the guest actually uses, for example EFT, and note it on the cash-up sheet. |
| **Floats**                   | No float is issued to any terminal and the Admin Cashup float must be R0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Cash payouts**             | Suppliers are never paid from a till. Capture supplier invoices with their real payment method (section 9).                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **IOU / staff loans**        | Not used. No money is lent to staff through Pilot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **POS cash station cash-up** | Not used, because no station holds a cash drawer with takings.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

### Tips

- Pelagos pays staff 100% of their tips.
- Card tips are totalled automatically by the POS, but the Retained Tips figure has to be typed in manually at cash-up. Copy the POS total exactly. If it is typed in lower than the POS total, the day looks over.
- Retained Tips are tip money kept for staff, not banked as business income.
- Any difference found later is corrected on the tips sheet, so staff are always paid correctly.

## 6. TOUCH POS: WAITRON PROCEDURES

> **Own login only.** Every waitron logs in with their own fingerprint, or their own card where fingerprints are not set up. Never use another person’s login and never let anyone use yours. Clock in and out with the Pilot fingerprint scanner as set out in the Staff Handbook (PEL-POL-001, section 4.4).

### Opening a table

1.  Log in to Pilot Touch POS with your fingerprint.
2.  Enter the table number on the number pad. For a Dineplan reservation, use the table allocated in Dineplan (PEL-SOP-003).
3.  Enter the number of guests (covers). Always enter the correct number, as covers feed the sales reports.
4.  Touch Yes to confirm that you are starting a new table.

If the system asks for covers when you expected an existing table, that table does not exist yet and you are starting a new one. Check the table number before continuing.

### Ordering items

1.  Select the menu category you want to order from.
2.  Touch the item, then Enter to add it to the table.
3.  Select every pop-up option that appears, for example how a steak is cooked or the choice of starch, so the kitchen or bar slip is complete.
4.  When the order is complete, touch Order to send it to the kitchen or bar printers.

Where management has loaded information on an item, such as allergens or the standard cocktail recipe, touch INFO and select the item to read it.

### Adding items to an open table

1.  Log in with your fingerprint.
2.  Select the table you want to add items to.
3.  Select the menu category and touch each item.
4.  Touch Order to confirm the order.

### Changing items before they are ordered

Items in red have been added but not yet ordered and can still be edited. Items in green have already been sent to a printer and can only be removed by a manager void (section 7). All deletions are logged in the audit file.

1.  Open the table.
2.  Touch Edit.
3.  Select the item and how many of it must be removed.
4.  Touch Delete.
5.  Touch OK when you have finished editing the bill.

### Splitting a bill

Create the splits as soon as guests ask for separate bills, before items are added.

1.  Select the table and touch Split. The Table Split / View screen opens.
2.  Touch New, then Split, and repeat until you have the number of splits you need.
3.  Select a split by touching its number (use the arrows to see more splits) and touch OK.
4.  Ring up the items for that split.
5.  Touch Split and select the next split for the next guest’s items.
6.  Touch Order when finished.

To scrap all splits, touch Split, then Reset, and confirm with Yes. All items move back to split one.

### Viewing, printing and closing a bill

1.  To check a bill, select the table and touch Enter, then Esc to return to the main screen.
2.  Touch Print and then the table number to print the pro-forma invoice for the guest to check.
3.  When the guest is ready to pay, take payment on the TABBS card machine. TABBS closes the table automatically and the final tax invoice prints.
4.  If TABBS took the payment but the table did not close, call the Duty Manager to close it with Tabbs Manual. Do not take the payment again.
5.  If the payment cannot go through TABBS (machine down, EFT, customer account, MaxiClub, voucher or Dineplan), call the Duty Manager, who checks the proof of payment and closes the bill with the correct payment type from section 5.
6.  To pay a split bill, touch Split at the tender screen, select the split (or the items) being paid, complete the payment and repeat until every split is paid. If one party leaves early, the outstanding balance stays on the table for later.

## 7. TOUCH POS: SUPERVISOR AND MANAGER FUNCTIONS

### Preventing theft and fraud through the POS

- Manage staff logins and PINs. Every staff member uses their own fingerprint or card whenever they are on duty. If a staff member has left their card at home, issue a new one.
- Manager cards, PINs and fingerprints authorise voids, discounts and transfers. Never leave a manager card unattended and never let any employee use your login.
- Authorise every void, discount and transfer yourself, at the terminal.
- Monitor rolling orders and tables that stay open for long periods.
- Keep transfers of tables and items between waitrons to a minimum. Frequent transfers and splits can be used to confuse bill totals, stock and cash-up. If you see a pattern, ask questions and monitor the staff member.
- Strictly manage order cancellations and corrections. Frequent corrections point either to an attempt to defraud the system or to a training need.
- Review voids, discounts, splits and transfers every day on the Day End report and the Discount Log.

### Floor plan and table status

1.  Touch Floor Plan or Open Tables and log in to display the Hosting window.
2.  Touch a table to see the waitron and table details. Use Open to view the table and Attention to flag a table whose waitron needs to attend to it.

| **Table colour** | **Meaning**                                |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| **Yellow**       | A new table, nothing has been ordered yet. |
| **Green**        | Items have been ordered for the table.     |
| **Pink**         | The bill has been printed.                 |
| **Red**          | The table needs attention.                 |

Pelagos takes reservations in Dineplan (PEL-SOP-003), not in Pilot’s Book function.

### Item availability and stock warnings

- **Out of stock:** in Pilot Admin, edit the PLU and tick Out of stock so waitrons cannot order it. Untick it as soon as stock arrives.
- **PLU stock warnings:** Manager Menu > Controls > PLU Stock Warning. Set the warnings and messages that show staff what is low or out of stock, update them every day and confirm the update when prompted on exit.
- **Stock (POS):** Manager Menu > Stock POS shows the stock available for sale at that terminal, for example a bar.

### Quick tables at a bar station

Where a bar station is set up with a quick table number, the quick table stays open all day and reopens automatically after each payment.

1.  Log in and enter the quick table number. The first time each day, confirm that it is a new table by touching Yes.
2.  Select the items, press Enter until the billing screen appears and take payment through TABBS, or select the correct payment type from section 5.
3.  Touch Enter to continue. The system reopens the quick table, ready for the next bill.

### Transferring items, tables and merging tables

### Items, same waitron:

1.  Log in as the waitron and touch Items.
2.  Touch Table and select the table to transfer from. The Table / Split View window opens.
3.  Enter how many of each item must move in the Selected column and touch OK.
4.  Select the receiving table, or enter a new table number and the covers.
5.  Confirm with Yes and authorise with your manager fingerprint, card or PIN.

**Items, different waitron:** follow the same steps, but when transferring to a new table also enter the receiving waitron’s number and the covers, then confirm with Yes and authorise.

### Whole table to another waitron or table:

1.  Log in to the Touch POS as a manager and touch Trans.
2.  Select the table to transfer from and authorise.
3.  Enter the new table number (and the waitron number where asked) and authorise again.
4.  Confirm the transfer with Yes.

**Merging tables:** use Trans in the same way, select the table to merge from, select the table to merge into, enter the waitron number, authorise each step and confirm with Yes.

### Discounts

Pilot allows a value or percentage discount on one item or on the whole bill, always with manager authorisation, and asks for a discount reason. Follow PEL-SOP-002 for complaint-related discounts and PEL-MAN-004: no complimentary item is given without the Duty Manager. Items given away with approval must still be rung up so the stock deducts.

### Discounting an item:

1.  Open the table and ring up the item.
2.  Before moving the item to the item list, touch Disc and authorise.
3.  For a value discount, touch Minus and enter the amount (it cannot be more than the item price). For a percentage discount, enter the percentage.
4.  Touch Order. If the item has already been ordered, void it first and then ring it up again with the discount.

### Discounting a bill:

1.  Bill the table and, at the tender stage, touch Disc and authorise.
2.  Enter the value (not more than the bill total) or the percentage.
3.  Touch Copy to print the tax invoice.

For tax reasons a discount cannot be given on a pro-forma invoice. The discounted bill completes as a tax invoice, so check that every item is correct first.

### Voiding items

A void is needed once items have been sent to an order printer or a pro-forma invoice has been printed.

1.  Open the table. Ordered items show in green.
2.  Touch Void and select the item (top left, in green).
3.  Authorise with your manager PIN, card or fingerprint.
4.  Select the reason for the void.
5.  The item now shows in red with a minus sign. Touch Exit or Order to complete the void.
6.  A void slip prints. The manager and the waitron sign it and it is attached to the Discount Log at the end of the day.
7.  When the table is opened again, the voided item shows in purple.

> **Voided items go back into stock.** If the item was made and wasted, ring it up again and discount it by 100% so the stock is deducted without charging the guest.

- Voids are always authorised by a manager, never done directly, so every void has two witnesses.
- Include the signed void slips in the cash-up and compare them against the bill printouts.
- File the slips with the Void / Discount report at the end of each day.

### Reprinting a closed bill

1.  Touch Closed Bills on the Pilot POS screen.
2.  Find the bill and touch Print.
3.  Select Slip Print. The bill prints.

Pilot keeps the day’s bills until Day End. Cashup and Day End reports of earlier days can be reprinted in Pilot Admin through Sales > Reprint.

### Take-away and delivery (only if set up)

The take-away and delivery waitron numbers must first be set up on the station (section 20). Both work like a quick table, but print a reference number on the order slip and on the receipt so bills can be matched to orders. For delivery, search for the customer by telephone number or surname, or touch Add to capture a new client. Notes added to a single order print on that order; notes saved on the client print on every order, so use them for permanent details such as directions.

### Online orders (only if enabled)

1.  Set up once: Manager Menu > Settings > POS/Printers, Options tab, tick Notify on New Sales Orders on every station that will manage online orders.
2.  New orders show on the Pilot home screen. Select Orders, then Online Orders.
3.  Pending orders show on the Pending tab. Select an order to see the items; use Show details for more information and Show Items to return.
4.  Select Accept or Reject.
5.  On the Accepted tab, mark the order Ready when it is ready for collection or delivery, or select Collect straight away.
6.  Collect opens the billing screen. An order paid online comes through as an approved payment: select Close Bill. If the customer pays on collection, process the payment as normal through TABBS.
7.  Collected and paid orders move to the Collected tab, delivered orders to the Delivered tab.

## 8. DAILY RESTAURANT CONTROL CYCLE

| **Time block**                 | **Pilot routine**                                                                                                                                | **Owner at Pelagos**                       |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| **Opening / morning**          | Start the system and check that the TABBS and backup card machines work. Record morning prep issues, bulk portioning and production estimates.   | Opening manager / Head Chef                |
| **During trade**               | Capture supplier invoices, issues, fills, production and operational changes as they happen. Authorise voids, discounts and transfers.           | Duty Manager / Head Chef / delegated admin |
| **Late afternoon / pre-close** | Cash off day shift waitrons who are not working the evening shift, finalise bulk portioning and capture issues, fills and outstanding purchases. | Closing Duty Manager / Head Chef           |
| **Close of trade**             | Capture closing counts, cash off waitrons, complete the Admin Cashup (payment types and retained tips) and run Day End.                          | Closing Duty Manager                       |
| **After Day End**              | Enter Prep estimates for the new day, print the Daily Orders report and the control sheets for the next day.                                     | Closing Duty Manager / Head Chef           |
| **Sunday 17:00**               | Weekly kitchen stock count and stock entry.                                                                                                      | Head Chef                                  |
| **Last day of month**          | Full stock count, report validation and GM pack.                                                                                                 | F&B Administrator                          |

> **Pelagos control rule.** No count is valid while stock is still moving. Whenever a stock routine is performed, sales, transfers, fills, issues and purchases must either already be recorded or physically paused until the count is complete.

### Close-of-trade sequence

1.  Capture any outstanding supplier invoices and print the Daily Purchases report (section 9).
2.  Complete the Production Module first, before the Bulk, Fruit and Veg, Dry Stocks and Prep sheets are closed (section 13).
3.  Count and capture the Fruit and Veg closing stock and print the usage sheet.
4.  Capture the bulk portioning information and print the Bulk Costing report.
5.  Capture Dry Stocks issues and closing stock and print the usage sheet.
6.  Capture Prep Sheet issues and closing stock (bar and kitchen), check the variances, recount where needed and print Prep Differences Only and Prep Sheet Totals.
7.  Make sure every table is closed and every waitron has been cashed off.
8.  Pull the Sales (X) reading.
9.  Complete the Admin Cashup (section 12).
10. Print the Discount Log and attach the signed void slips.
11. Exit all terminals to the Pilot shell program and run Day End.
12. After Day End, enter the estimates for the new day, print the Daily Orders report and print the count sheets for the next day.

## 9. PURCHASES AND SUPPLIER INVOICES

Every supplier invoice must be captured on the day it is received. Capturing an invoice increases the stock levels and updates the unit prices, so a wrong unit or VAT mode distorts stock values, costings and the Income Statement.

> **No cash purchases.** Pelagos holds no cash, so suppliers are never paid from a till and Pilot’s Cash Payout function is not used. Capture every invoice with its actual payment method (account or EFT). A cash payout or a cash purchase on any report is a capture error that must be corrected.

### Capturing a daily purchase invoice

1.  In Pilot Admin, select Purchases > Day Entry, or click the Purchases button.
2.  Click New, type the supplier’s name in the search block, select the supplier and click OK.
3.  In the payments frame, select how the invoice is paid (account or EFT) and enter the payment reference.
4.  Enter the invoice number in the Supplier’s Reference field so the invoice can be traced later.
5.  Confirm whether the invoice is VAT inclusive or exclusive and change the tax mode with F5 – Tax if needed.
6.  Enter the invoice total.
7.  Click Add and search for and select each item on the invoice.
8.  Enter the quantity in the same unit as the Master File, and the line cost if it has changed since the last purchase.
9.  Confirm that the system total balances to the invoice total.
10. Click Exit. Print the purchase as proof of capture if required and file it with the invoice.

If a supplier delivers a different size from the Master File unit, convert the quantity. For example, if Jameson is set up as a 750 ml bottle (factor 30 tots) and a 1 litre bottle is delivered, capture 1.33 bottles.

### Correcting invoices

- **Edit an item:** open the invoice, click Edit, make the change and click Exit.
- **Edit the invoice number or payment reference:** select the invoice, click Ref, make the change and click OK.
- **Delete an item:** open the invoice, select the item, click Delete, confirm and click Exit.
- **Delete an invoice:** select the invoice, click Delete, confirm and click Exit.

### Batch (back-dated) and expense purchases

- **Batch purchases** (Purchases > Batch) post an invoice to a date up to 60 days back, for example an expense that belongs to the previous month. They do not update stock levels or control sheets, because the stock may already be sold. Use them only for invoices that belong to an earlier period. They show on the Day End report and on the Batch Details report.
- **Future purchases** work like daily purchases but only accept expense items, such as rent and salaries, not food cost items.

### Purchase reports (Purchases > Reports)

Print the Daily Purchases report every day after all invoices have been captured.

| **Report**                                | **Use**                                                                                                                   |
|-------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Payment Type Summary**                  | Purchases by payment type (cash, cheque, account and EFT), with categories and VAT. At Pelagos the cash line must be nil. |
| **Invoice Summary**                       | The day’s invoices by supplier, reference and cost. Check that every invoice received was captured.                       |
| **Category Summary**                      | Purchases by category, regardless of payment type.                                                                        |
| **Inv/Cat Summary**                       | Each invoice broken down into categories.                                                                                 |
| **VAT Report**                            | All VAT for the selected period.                                                                                          |
| **Price Variance (last 3 price updates)** | The last three price changes on an item. Use it to spot supplier price increases and capture errors.                      |
| **Batch Details**                         | All back-dated invoices.                                                                                                  |
| **Payments**                              | Purchases listed by payment type.                                                                                         |

## 10. DAILY CONTROL SHEETS

Pilot has four daily control sheets plus the Production Module. Production must always be completed before the other sheets are closed, because produced items change the stock on them.

| **Sheet**               | **What goes on it**                                                                | **What it gives you**                                                                    |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Prep Sheet**          | Items that must be watched closely: bar front stock, portions and controlled prep. | Daily usage, variances (short or over) and prep estimates.                               |

## 11. DAILY BAR STOCK TAKE SOP

### Objective

The daily bar stock take is Pelagos’ primary front-stock control. It is used to compare what should remain in front stock after sales and fills against what is physically left at closing. The physical counting rules are set out in PEL-SOP-005 Bar Stock Take.

### Scope

- All spirits lines
- All wines in service stock
- All draught products
- High-risk bar consumables that Pelagos chooses to control on the Prep Sheet, such as mixers or bottled products.

### Counting standard

- Count in the same unit that appears in Pilot.
- For sealed bottles, count actual bottle quantities.
- For open bottles, use the stock measure circles provided, or the Stock Mate scale where it is used (section 10).
- For draught, use the approved keg or litre method and keep that method consistent from day to day.
- Do not change measurement logic between shifts or between managers.

### Step-by-step physical count process

1.  At close, stop all bar sales and close any active bills before the count begins.
2.  One bartender counts and calls; the second person records; the Closing Duty Manager verifies high-value lines.
3.  Flag damaged, leaking, spoiled or breakage items separately. Do not hide them inside the closing quantity.
4.  Sign the physical count sheet once finished.

### Pilot capture by the Closing Duty Manager

Pilot’s daily-routines material places day-end stock control around the Prep Sheet and associated front-stock routines. Where Pelagos’ bar items are managed through the Prep Sheet, the Closing Duty Manager must use that structure; where a formal back-stock count is required, the count is entered via Stock Entry after the relevant date close.

1.  Open Pilot Admin.
2.  Go to Controls > Prep Sheet for bar-controlled front stock items.
3.  Confirm that all bar fills/issues for the day have already been entered in the FILL column.
4.  Move to the Close tab and enter the physical closing counts for each controlled bar item, or import them from the Stock Mate scale (section 10).
5.  Review the Diff column for shorts or overs.
6.  Print the Prep Differences Only report.
7.  Print the Prep Sheet Totals report for the day.
8.  If Pelagos is using stock points for multiple bar selling locations, confirm the counts were entered under the correct stock point.

### Daily submission

1.  Attach the signed physical bar count sheet.
2.  Attach the Prep Differences report and Prep Totals report.
3.  Write a brief variance note for any line over the site tolerance.
4.  Email or file the daily bar pack to the F&B Administrator before the manager signs off Day End.
5.  Escalate immediately to the GM if there is an unexplained major variance in premium spirits, wine or draught.

## 12. CLOSING DUTY MANAGER: WAITER CASH-UP, ADMIN CASHUP AND DAY END

> **No cash at cash-up.** Pelagos is cashless, so there is no cash to count, no float to issue or carry forward and no cash payout to reconcile. The cash-up reconciles TABBS and the other payment types in section 5, plus the retained tips.

### What Pilot expects before Admin Cashup

Pilot’s daily-routines module states that Admin Cashup is performed after each POS station and staff member has been cashed up and after the manager has gathered all supporting information.

| **Required before starting Admin Cashup**                                                                    | **Why it matters**                                                                                     |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **All tables closed, including any TABBS payment that did not close its table (close it with Tabbs Manual)** | Pilot will not cash off a waitron who has open tables, and Day End will not run while tables are open. |
| **Signed waiter cash-up slips**                                                                              | Support each waitron’s sales, payment types and tips.                                                  |
| **TABBS totals**                                                                                             | Validate the main card machine settlements (Approved Payments).                                        |
| **FNB backup machine slips and batch total**                                                                 | Support any Credit Card (C/CARD) payments, which must be typed in manually.                            |
| **EFT proofs of payment and customer account bills**                                                         | Support EFT and account payments.                                                                      |
| **MaxiClub, voucher and Dineplan references**                                                                | Support the non-card payment types.                                                                    |
| **Tip totals from the POS**                                                                                  | Needed to type in Retained Tips exactly.                                                               |
| **Total sales / X reading**                                                                                  | Provides a sales reference for reconciliation.                                                         |
| **Signed void slips and the Discount Log**                                                                   | Support every void and discount.                                                                       |

### Cashing off a waitron

1.  Touch Manager Menu > Waiter Cashup, or Reports > Waiter > Commission and then Cashup.
2.  Select the waitron and touch OK to open the Waiter Cashup window.
3.  Check the payment types the waitron closed against the TABBS record and the slips and proofs. No cash is collected, because none is taken.
4.  Confirm the waitron’s tip total.
5.  Touch Print and choose the printout that lists all bills closed by the waitron, with discounts and tips. The waitron signs the slip.

Pilot will not cash off a waitron who has open tables, and once cashed off the waitron cannot log in again until Day End. The payment types drawn into the waitron cash-up are for reference only; always check them against actual proof, such as card machine slips.

**Un-cashing a waitron who must come back on duty:** select Waiter Cashup and the waitron, click OK on the message that they have been paid, remove the figures, click Print and confirm with Yes. When the waitron is cashed up again later, add the earlier figures to the new cash-up.

Print the Waiter Commission report once all staff have been cashed off. It shows sales, tips and the payment breakdown for each staff member and supports the tip pay-over.

### Admin Cashup step by step

1.  Make sure every waitron and POS terminal that should be closed has already been cashed off.
2.  Gather the items listed above.
3.  Open Pilot Admin and click Cashup.
4.  Check the float. Pelagos holds no float, so it must be R0. If a float shows, right-click the Cashup Summary option and select Reset Float.
5.  Check the Approved Payments figure. It is TABBS card payments plus customer account payments, added together automatically. Nothing else counts unless it is typed in.
6.  Type in every payment type that does not come in automatically, exactly as per the slips and proofs: Credit Card (C/CARD) from the FNB backup machine, EFT, MaxiClub, Voucher and Dineplan.
7.  Type in Retained Tips, copying the POS tip total exactly.
8.  Click Summary and review the Variance field. The variance is the gap between the cash-up total and the day’s actual turnover.
9.  If the variance is not zero, work through the patterns in the table below before continuing. Do not simply force the close.
10. Use the banking function to bank all payment types. Nothing is carried forward, because there is no float.
11. Print the Cashup Summary. The cash-up can be locked to stop others editing it before Day End. Close the cash-up once a day only, not at the end of each shift.
12. Record the day on the cash-up sheet, with a note for any variance.

### Why the numbers sometimes do not match

Almost every gap fits one of these patterns. None of them means money has gone missing. The money is accounted for; it has just landed somewhere unexpected in the POS’s own categories.

| **Pattern**                               | **What happened**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | **What to check**                                                                                             |
|-------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Backup or manual card payment**         | The main card reader is down, so payment is taken on the backup machine or entered manually. The money is real, but it does not land in the POS’s usual card-sales figure, so it has to be added back in manually at cash-up. This is the most common reason a day looks short.          | The FNB batch total is typed in under Credit Card.                                                            |
| **Card declined, guest pays another way** | A declined card still needs the bill closed there and then, so staff used a placeholder (until now, Cheque) while the guest arranged another way to pay, often EFT. The money does arrive, but the POS shows it as paid by cheque.                                                       | Match the EFT when it arrives and note it on the sheet.                                                       |
| **Tip-retention gap**                     | Card tips are totalled automatically by the POS but typed in manually at cash-up. Done imprecisely, the retained-tip figure comes in lower than the POS total, making the day look over. No money is missing and staff are still paid correctly, as this is corrected on the tips sheet. | Retype the exact POS tip total.                                                                               |
| **Payment toward a customer account**     | A payment toward a running account used to come in by card but was not recorded as a normal table sale, so it could look separate from the day’s figures. Going forward these are paid by EFT.                                                                                           | Confirm the EFT and the account it belongs to.                                                                |
| **A card payment with no bill attached**  | A card payment goes through but is never linked to a POS bill, for example an advance event payment. The POS sales figure is short by the same amount, so no variance shows, but the money is not counted as a sale anywhere. This is the hardest to catch.                              | The Card Machine Cross-Check tab of the monthly workbook, line by line against the TABBS portal (section 23). |
| **A one-off POS mistake**                 | A single clear slip: the wrong amount typed in, a payment processed twice or a bill closed incorrectly. It is tied to one bill and one staff member.                                                                                                                                     | The bill and the staff member concerned.                                                                      |

### Day End step by step

1.  Confirm all other terminals are logged out to the main shell program.
2.  Confirm there are no open tables. Pilot will not allow Day End to continue if open tables remain.
3.  Access Pilot Admin.
4.  Go to Controls > Day End.
5.  Confirm you want to continue. Pilot will run a table rebuild.
6.  Review the day summary shown by the system.
7.  Enter the actual sales (the actual turnover from the Admin Cashup) if it differs from the displayed amount.
8.  Close and confirm the process.
9.  Allow Pilot to close the Prep Sheet automatically if it has not yet been closed.
10. Review the Day End report immediately after it prints, focusing on security breaches, the total sales breakdown, department sales, time sales, PLU sales, batch purchases, table and item transfers and waiter sales. The cash payouts listing must be empty.

## 17. VARIANCE HANDLING AND INVESTIGATION

Pilot’s reporting and stock-control material is designed to show shorts, overs and the gap between actual and theoretical usage. Pelagos must treat variance review as a formal management process, not a filing exercise.

| **Variance type**                     | **First action**                                                                                                                                                                      | **Escalation**                                    |
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **Small, explainable timing issue**   | Annotate and monitor next cycle.                                                                                                                                                      | Escalate only if repeated.                        |
| **Unexplained bar shortage**          | Immediate recount and review of fills, transfers, comps, voids and ringing.                                                                                                           | Notify F&B Administrator and GM if material.      |
| **Kitchen overuse**                   | Check recipe quantities, yields, portioning, wastage log and production records.                                                                                                      | Escalate to Head Chef and GM if trend repeats.    |
| **Bulk loss**                         | Check issued weights, pack loss, portion counts and purchase units, which all affect the Bulk Variance report.                                                                        | Head Chef; GM if repeated.                        |
| **Unusual theoretical vs actual gap** | Review PLU costings, prep links, production setup and stock units.                                                                                                                    | F&B Administrator to open corrective action item. |
| **Cash-up variance**                  | Work through the payment variance patterns in section 12: backup card payments, declined cards, retained tips, account payments, card payments with no bill and one-off POS mistakes. | GM if unresolved at close.                        |

### Mandatory variance workflow

1.  Identify the exact item, date and amount of the variance.
2.  Check whether the issue is quantity, price, unit, linkage or timing related.
3.  Recount if the item is material or high risk.
4.  Review source transactions: purchases, fills, payment types, voids, discounts, stock points, production runs or recipe changes.
5.  Document the explanation and corrective action.
6.  Assign an owner and a due date where the variance indicates a process problem.
7.  Report repeated or serious variances to the GM.

1.  Click New after choosing an unused CAT code, enter the code, description, CODE and cost centre and click OK. Pilot warns if the code or description already exists.

3.  A category with Master File items linked to it cannot be deleted. Move the items to the correct category first.
4.  On exit, Pilot warns of any duplicate codes or descriptions.

### Master file item creation and linking

Every new purchase item, expense item, portion item and raw-recipe item must be created correctly in the Master File before it is used in purchasing, production, prep sheets or PLU costing.

1.  Go to Admin > Files > Master File and click Find first to confirm the item does not already exist.
2.  If the item does not exist, click New and complete the description with a clear naming format that any manager can understand, for example "Meat – sirloin – bulk" or "Meat – sirloin 200g".
3.  Select the correct category, then select the correct control sheet from the dropdown. The control sheet must match the way Pelagos intends to control the item: Prep, Bulk, none, or other approved control sheet.
4.  Enter the count unit exactly as the item will be counted: KG, LT or EACH. Enter the ex-VAT unit cost and the physical location where the item is stored.
5.  Change the tax code to non-vatable only where the item is genuinely non-vatable. Tick Purchase Item where the item will ever be loaded from an invoice or supplier purchase.
6.  Click OK only once all required fields are complete.

| **Count sheet** | **Use it for**                                                                                                                                                                |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **PREP**        | Daily control items.                                                                                                                                                          |
| **BULK**        | Items bought in bulk and converted into smaller sellable portions, for example rump bought per kilogram and portioned into 350 g steaks (the portions themselves go on PREP). |
| **FVEG**        | Fruit and vegetables.                                                                                                                                                         |
| **DRYSTOCK**    | Other countable items, for example dairy, cleaning materials, packaging and recipe items such as sauces.                                                                      |
| **NONE**        | Items that cannot be counted, for example salaries, water and electricity.                                                                                                    |

- Units are KG, LITRE or EACH, or PORTION for portion items. Any purchase size can be converted to one of these units.
- The unit cost is the ex-VAT price per stated unit. If the price is not known yet, R1 can be entered for now; the cost updates to real prices as invoices are captured.
- The cost of a recipe item, such as a sauce, is calculated by the system once its R/M costing has been entered.
- Tick Daily Order and complete the order levels where the item must appear on the daily or weekly orders (sections 10 and 14).

### Prep Sheet rules

- Do not change a prep item DPT code after it has been linked to a PLU; Pilot warns that the link will be lost and stock will stop deducting correctly.
- Use the CONTROL field for items where variances must be visible.
- Use PCON = Y for items controlled by stock point across multiple selling locations.
- Use BSTK = Y where items must first sit in back stock before being issued to front stock.
- Set the FACTOR correctly for portion conversions, for example, tots per bottle or slices per cake.
- If closing counts are inaccurate, the AVG and estimate logic will also be inaccurate.

### Prep Sheet setup for new items

After a Master File item is linked to the Prep Sheet, open Files > Prep Sheet and complete the blank fields for the new item.

1.  Set Code to determine the print order, GRP to determine the printed page grouping, and CONTROL to Y where the item must appear on the variance report. Use N only where management has approved that variances on the item do not need to show.
2.  Use PCON where the item must be controlled in more than one stock point, for example where multiple bars sell the same line from different terminals.
3.  Use BSTK = Y where stock sits in a back stock location before being issued to front stock. Leave blank or set N where the item goes directly to sale.
4.  Set FACTOR very carefully so Pilot converts the purchase unit into the selling or issuing unit correctly, for example one bottle of spirits to 30 tots. A wrong factor will create false variances and misleading usage reports.
- **Grouping:** with basic grouping, the count sheet prints by GRP number and then by CODE (for example soft drinks on group 1, beers on group 2), so leave gaps between codes for future items. Pilot support can switch on DPTGROUP so the GRP column follows the order of the fridges, for example 1-001, 1-002 and 1-003.
- **H/PREP:** tick only for items produced hourly; Pilot then estimates what to produce per hour.
- **Hiding items:** right-click an item with a star and select Hide Item. Items holding stock cannot be hidden. A hidden item stays in the Master File and can still be ordered and purchased. Use Show All Items (hidden items show in yellow) and Show Item to unhide.
- **Links:** select the prep item and click Link to see every PLU linked to it. Click Add, select the PLU and enter the factor, the number of portions that deduct when the PLU sells. Weight-based items take up to three decimals, for example 0.125 for 125 g of chicken strips. Delete removes a wrong link and Print L prints all prep to PLU links.

### Stock points for Pelagos bars

Pilot’s Stock Point Setup guide is designed for venues with two or more bar areas. If Pelagos sells the same items from multiple front-stock locations, stock points should be enabled so issues, sales, usage and variances can be seen by selling location.

1.  In Files > Prep Sheet, set PCON = Y for the relevant prep items.
2.  In Files > Stock Points, set the number of stock points required and rename them clearly.
3.  At each POS terminal, go through Manager Menu > Setup > Pos/Printers and assign the correct stock point.
4.  Test that sales on each terminal deduct from the correct stock point before going live.

### Bulk sheet setup

Where a Master File item must be portioned, go to Admin > Files > Bulk Sheet, select the item from the bulk list, and on the right choose whether the bulk item preps to a sellable portion item or moves to another bulk item. This must be maintained carefully for off-cuts and portion conversion control.

- Use +Prep to link each portion (prep item) and +Bulk to link another bulk item, for example hake off-cuts kept for fish stock.
- Set PRNT to N for bulk items that are not portioned but only used to make other items, so they do not print on the Bulk Portion Sheet.
- The bulk item and all its portions must exist in the Master File first. A bulk item has no other ingredients; once two or more ingredients are combined it is a production item (Production Manager). A produced item can itself be portioned on the Bulk Sheet.
- Items with a star can be hidden in the same way as on the Prep Sheet.

Go to Admin > Files > PLU Items to create or maintain the selling item.

2.  Create the PLU and complete the PLU code, name, selling price, department, printing destination and meal type where integration requires it.
3.  Use the Link function in the PLU file to attach the PLU to the correct Prep Sheet item or items so sales deduct the right stock. Confirm the factor on each link.

### Meal types

Meal types show how many main meals are sold and which waitrons are upselling, through the Main Meal Comparatives report.

1.  Go to Files > Meal Types and click New.
2.  Enter the meal type, tick Main Meal if it counts as a main meal and tick Reverse Ratio only if the report must be read the other way round (extras per main meal instead of main meals per extra).
3.  Click OK.
4.  In Files > PLU Items, edit each PLU, select its meal type and enter the Main Meal Multiplier.

A meal type with PLUs allocated to it cannot be deleted; move the PLUs first.

### Add / Remove items

Add / Remove lets guests remove ingredients from a meal for a set price reduction and add extras for a set charge, while keeping stock correct.

1.  Create every ingredient that may be added or removed as a PLU first, with its PLU costing and, if it is a prep item, its PLU to Prep link and factor.
2.  Go to Files > Add/Remove Items and select the Main PLU (filter by department if needed).
3.  Check the linked prep items, then open the PLU Search tab and click Edit.
4.  Select the PLUs that may be removed (hold Shift to select several), click in the Items that may be Removed box and enter the price to deduct for each.
5.  Select the PLUs that may be added, click in the Items that may be Added box and enter the price to add for each.
6.  Click Save, then Exit. Undo reverses unsaved changes and Delete removes a linked item. Right-click Copy and Paste copies the links from one Main PLU to another.

### Set menus with PLU limits

Campaign Manager is the preferred way to run set menus. Where a set menu must be built on a Master PLU instead:

1.  Create the Master PLU (for example a Valentine’s Day menu) and tick Set Menu Item.
2.  Create each slave PLU and assign it to a set menu group, for example STARTERS, MAINS and DESSERTS.
3.  In the PLU grid, select the Master PLU and click PLU Limit. Tick Set menu and confirm with Yes to make it the Set Menu Master.
4.  Click Add, select each slave PLU, choose its mode and enter how many may be ordered from its group. Use No Charge mode where the price sits on the Master PLU. Click Link.

### PLU Costings and recipe maintenance

Pilot states that PLU Costings is where recipes are created for all PLU items and that these costings are vital for Raw Material Usage and Theoretical Sales reports.

1.  Open Costing > PLU Costing.
2.  Search for the PLU item and confirm the standard recipe ingredients.
3.  Add every standard ingredient used in the item.
4.  Enter quantities in the correct units.
5.  Set options/modifiers separately where they are not standard ingredients.
6.  Where items follow a similar recipe, use Pilot’s copy approach carefully and then verify each copied item.
7.  Review target GP percentages and update when menu prices or ingredient costs change.
- Enter quantities in the Master File unit: 140 g of an item kept in kilograms is 0.140.
- Cost a PLU to the portioned or produced ingredient (for example the 200 g fillet portion), not to the bulk purchase item, because the costs differ.
- Load non-standard ingredients in the option windows, for example option 1 for the choice of starch and option 2 for the choice of sauce. Use Print Options to see the full cost including options.
- Enter a target GP% or C.O.S.% in the Target window. The Actual window shows cost, GP%, C.O.S.% and markup, and turns red when the target is missed. Targets also give a recommended selling price for a new PLU.
- Before printing costing reports, answer Yes when asked to update the costings.

### PLU costing and raw material costing

In Admin > Costing > PLU Costing, add every ingredient that appears on the plate, including garnish, and enter the exact quantity used per dish. This drives the individual PLU cost of sale.

In Admin > Costing > R/M Costing, add the recipe for any produced or prepped Master File item, such as a lamb curry or sauce. Quantities must reflect the output unit of the completed item, for example the ingredients needed to make one kilogram of the finished item.

### Production and bulk items

- Use the Bulk Sheet only where a purchased bulk item is portioned into saleable items without other ingredients.
- Use Production Manager where multiple ingredients are combined to produce a new item, such as sauces or prepared components.
1.  In Admin, open Production.
2.  Select Setup and add the production master item.
3.  Enter the quantity produced by the recipe.
4.  Add each ingredient detail item and enter its recipe quantity.
5.  Save the production recipe and use Production daily as part of kitchen preparation.

### Campaign Manager setup for specials and set menus

Campaign Manager allows Pelagos to run specials and set menus without creating duplicate PLUs for every promotion.

1.  Go to Pilot Admin > Files > Campaign Manager and create the Campaign from the Campaign Setup tab. Enter the campaign name, description, invoice-printing option and any excluded order types, then save.
2.  From the Order Rule Setup tab create the order rule that explains how the campaign works. Choose whether the guest must buy one of each item or any quantity from a list, whether a cheapest or most expensive item becomes free, or whether a set value, discount amount or discount percentage applies.

- Keep supplier details, including email addresses for emailed orders, up to date in the suppliers file.

Staff clock in and out with the Pilot fingerprint scanner in line with the Staff Handbook (PEL-POL-001, section 4.4), and the POPIA consent form PEL-FRM-002 is signed before a fingerprint is registered. - Gift Card List and Reprint Invoice: gift card activity and invoices to reprint.

### Other Pilot Admin reports (Reports menu)

- Turnover Breakdown (sit-down versus take-away) and Turnover Comparison (periods, covers, averages and budget).
- PLU Time Sales, Time Sales Analysis, Department Sales and Revenue per Department.
- Meal Type, Ticket Claims and Gift Card Transactions.
- Reprint of Cashup and Day End reports for earlier days (Sales > Reprint).
- Stock Turn Ratio: the average number of days it takes to turn stock.
- Pop Link List: how items are linked to pop-up screens.
- Cash Payouts, IOU / Loan and Airtime reports are not used at Pelagos. Any figure on them must be investigated.

### Raw Material Usage report: how to read it

Pilot explains that the Raw Material Usage report compares actual stock usage from physical counts with theoretical usage calculated from recipe costings multiplied by quantities sold.

- Use it after weekly and month-end counts, not as a substitute for counts.
- If the gap is large, investigate both operations and system setup.
- A bad recipe setup can look like wastage; real wastage can also look like a recipe issue. Check both.
- Review high-value proteins, liquor and recurring problem items first.
- Update the raw material costs and PLU costings before printing it.

### Income Statement: how to read and check it

The Income Statement works from one stock period to the next, so complete the stock routines and capture all purchases for the period first. Total sales exclude the opening date’s turnover and include the closing date’s, because stock files are for the end of each day’s trading.

- **Columns:** Cost % (share of cost of sales), Budget (target %), Var (difference from budget), Open and Close (stock values), Purch (purchases) and C/CNT (cost centre).
- **Codes:** D is cost of sales, E is expenses and X is excluded. A name showing ＊＊＊ is a deleted category that still has stock or purchases against it.
- **Closing or opening stock looks wrong:** check total values, unit prices and quantities in the stock files.
- **Purchases look wrong:** check that every invoice for the period was posted, with the right values and units.
- **Setup:** check every category has the correct code and that no undefined (＊＊＊) category remains.
- **Turnover:** net turnover must equal the Turnover Listing for the same period, and the default VAT percentage must be correct.

## 23. GM REPORT PACK

### Daily exception reporting to GM

- Only send daily reports to the GM when there is a significant unresolved bar shortage, cash-up variance or procedural breach.

## 24. NON-COMPLIANCE RULES

- No cash may be accepted from a customer, and no cash tender, float, cash payout or staff IOU may be processed in Pilot.
- No one may use another person’s login, PIN, card or fingerprint.
- No void may be processed without manager authorisation and a void slip signed by the manager and the waitron.
- No cash-up may be closed with an unexplained variance; every non-zero variance needs a note.
- No stock take may be marked complete if physical count sheets are unsigned.
- No manager may submit a stock file without reviewing variances.
- No unexplained premium-liquor shortage may be rolled forward without documented investigation.
- No month-end may be treated as final until the F&B Administrator has checked units, values and major exceptions.
- Repeated failure to follow the routine must be treated as a performance and accountability issue, not an admin issue.

## 26. APPENDIX B: GLOSSARY OF PILOT AND PELAGOS TERMS

| **Term**                           | **What it means**                                                                                                                                                                |
|------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Admin Cashup**                   | The daily reconciliation of the whole trading period, done after all waitrons and stations have been cashed off. At Pelagos it covers payment types and retained tips, not cash. |
| **Approved Payments**              | TABBS card payments plus customer account payments, added together automatically. Nothing else counts unless typed in manually at cash-up.                                       |
| **AVG**                            | The Prep Sheet column showing average usage per R1 000 of turnover, used for estimates.                                                                                          |
| **Back stock**                     | Pre-portioned or packed stock in storage, ready to be issued to front stock.                                                                                                     |
| **Batch purchases**                | Invoices posted up to 60 days back. They do not update stock levels.                                                                                                             |
| **Bulk stock**                     | Stock received in a bulk unit and portioned before use, for example heads of rump bought per kilogram.                                                                           |
| **Bulk Variance**                  | Losses on bulk and back stock, comparing actual stock with theoretical stock.                                                                                                    |
| **C/CARD**                         | A card payment entered manually from the backup FNB machine, rather than through TABBS.                                                                                          |
| **CASH**                           | Not accepted. Pelagos is cashless and will never take cash from a customer.                                                                                                      |
| **Cash up / Cash up Report**       | Produced when the POS is closed off at night. Shows total takings split by payment type, card, tips, EFT and so on.                                                              |
| **CHEQUE**                         | Never an actual cheque. A placeholder used until now to close a bill while a guest arranged to pay another way, usually EFT.                                                     |
| **Controls**                       | Pilot’s name for the daily, weekly and monthly routines and control sheets.                                                                                                      |
| **Customer Account**               | A running account some guests, usually owners, keep instead of paying per visit.                                                                                                 |
| **Day End / Day End Report**       | The routine that closes the trading day and its automatic, detailed report of every sale, payment and tip. It resets the POS for the next day.                                   |
| **DPT code**                       | The unique code of a prep item that links it to its PLUs.                                                                                                                        |
| **Factor**                         | The number of selling portions in one Master File unit, for example 30 tots in a 750 ml bottle.                                                                                  |
| **Fills**                          | Stock issued and prepped for the day, entered in the Fill column of the Prep Sheet.                                                                                              |
| **Forever Facilities FNB machine** | The backup card machine used when TABBS is down.                                                                                                                                 |
| **Front stock**                    | Stock available for immediate use in the kitchen or bar, counted daily.                                                                                                          |
| **Income Statement**               | Pilot’s summary of net sales, cost of sales, gross profit, expenses and net profit for a stock period.                                                                           |
| **Master File**                    | The file of every stock, purchase, recipe and expense item. The starting point for all setup.                                                                                    |
| **Modifier / descriptive item**    | A PLU that describes how an item is made, such as no onion, priced at R0.01 and printed with the item.                                                                           |
| **PLU**                            | Price of Listed Unit: a selling (menu) item.                                                                                                                                     |
| **PLU Costings**                   | The recipe of a PLU, which gives its cost of sale.                                                                                                                               |
| **Pop-up screen**                  | A screen of options that opens when certain PLUs are ordered, for example steak temperatures.                                                                                    |
| **Prep Sheet**                     | The main daily stock control sheet, showing issues, closing stock, usage and variances.                                                                                          |
| **Raw Material Usage**             | The report comparing actual usage from counts with theoretical usage from recipes and sales.                                                                                     |
| **Retained Tips**                  | Tip money kept for staff, not banked as business income. Typed in manually at cash-up.                                                                                           |
| **Stock point**                    | A selling location, such as a bar, controlled separately on the Prep Sheet.                                                                                                      |
| **TABBS**                          | The POS name for a card payment taken on the restaurant’s main card machine, the normal way most money comes in.                                                                 |
| **Tabbs Manual**                   | The payment type used when TABBS took the payment but did not close the table.                                                                                                   |
| **Touch Group**                    | A set of PLUs opened from one POS button.                                                                                                                                        |
| **Turnover / Sales**               | The day’s actual food and drink revenue, tips excluded. Everything else should add up to this figure.                                                                            |
| **Variance (cash-up)**             | The gap between the Cash up Report total and the day’s actual turnover. It must be explained whenever it is not zero.                                                            |
| **X reading**                      | The Sales (X) report: up-to-date turnover for the day so far.                                                                                                                    |
